quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must stay within the speed limit.
Must ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete a pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Before riding with a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you do.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold your waist, hips, or belt with a firm grip.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on, along with your running lights if you have them. Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is safe and legal.

questions.question: It is illegal to ride a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.
0.3 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone 21 or older cannot ride with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Anyone under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Riding may be unsafe even below the legal limit.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists rides together:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should ride near the front.
Inexperienced riders should ride in the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front.
questions.explanation: Place less experienced riders near the front of the group, behind the leader. This lets experienced riders lead and watch the newer riders at the same time.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay within the posted speed limit.
Exceed the speed limit by up to 10 mph to finish passing.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Complete all passes within the legal speed limit. Pass only where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
The roadway under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Traction may be poor on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement. Also avoid gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, you should ride in:

options.text: A single-file formation.
Pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A difference between goggles and a windshield is:

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but a windshield doesn't.
A windshield protects your eyes from the wind, but goggles don't.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but a windshield doesn't.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, push gently on the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any type of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any type of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any type of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: If you are passing parked vehicles on your right and there is no oncoming traffic on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid open car doors and people stepping out from between parked vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane to have more space around you.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Always use both the front and rear brakes when you stop.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip over. Instead, use the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you are most comfortable.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: The left portion of the lane is the safest when passing parked cars. This position helps you avoid open doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to change position if traffic or road conditions change.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Move only your head and eyes, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is in the left part of a lane, next to the centerline.
Is in the right part of a lane, next to the curb.
Can change depending on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change depending on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes depending on traffic and road conditions. Choose the position that gives you the best visibility and the most space around you. Move to a new position when conditions change.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how fast it is consumed. How often a person drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket for protection while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket protects you in a crash, regardless of weather. Jackets also help prevent dehydration in hot weather. Many riding jackets are designed to keep you from overheating.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when the motorcycle turns or leans.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when the motorcycle turns or leans.
questions.explanation: Before the passenger gets on, ask them to look over your shoulder in the direction you are turning. This helps you and the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions while riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride with caution when approaching an intersection. Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and both brakes so you can stop quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: How should you brake during a normal stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: During a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together and shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: Is it good to change your lane position?

options.text: No, because you will not get used to your lane.
No, because it confuses other drivers.
Yes, if conditions on the road are changing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if conditions on the road are changing.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as the road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast and how far away a small vehicle like a motorcycle is. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles will see you or understand your speed.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a passenger vehicle's brake light.

options.text: More noticeable than
Just as noticeable as
Not as noticeable as

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle's brake light is usually not as easy to see as a larger vehicle's brake light, especially when your taillight is on. Other drivers may not notice when you brake.

questions.question: What should you do if you shift gears while turning?

options.text: Only do it if you can shift smoothly.
It is better than shifting before the turn.
It is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only do it if you can shift smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause it to skid.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least how far behind the vehicle ahead?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist should keep at least a two-second distance behind other vehicles in normal conditions. If conditions are not perfect, use a larger distance.

questions.question: When rain starts, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the center of lanes when rain first starts. Ride in the tire tracks made by other vehicles. The left track is often safest.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely need to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Keep tire pressure the same.
Raise the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Raise the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure to use.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is the minimum following distance?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark. Use a three-second following distance when riding at night.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is okay to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, where should it be placed?

options.text: Over the rear axle.
On the gas tank in front of you.
Against the back seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Place loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: When parked on the road, how should a motorcycle be positioned?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
Without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: Park a motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: What is a sign that your front tire is flat?

options.text: Steering feels heavy.
Steering feels loose.
Steering feels soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering feels heavy.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: The front brake gives about what percentage of a motorcycle's total stopping power?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the total stopping power.
